metadata.title: The Planet Express Ship, Walked Through
metadata.render_by: Professor Bear, with his own tools (film source only)

beats.narration_text: This is Liam. This is the Planet Express ship, round 15, built by Grok Bot in Blender. Let's walk around it, view by view: what's there, what it shows, and where it still falls short.
beats.on_screen: Brutalist opening over the hero render

beats.narration_text: Front three-quarter. The rounded teal nose, the red lip wrapping it, the low dark-teal visor, and a row of cream portholes running back toward the turret.
beats.on_screen: Front three-quarter, slow push toward the visor
beats.label: nose, lip, visor

beats.narration_text: The right side tells you the silhouette. Turret on top, four portholes, the hatch, the ribbed cream vent, the swept fin with its logo, the wing, and the engine at the back.
beats.on_screen: Right side, pan nose to tail
beats.label: turret, portholes, vent, fin, engine

beats.narration_text: From the left, the logo reads the right way round, as it does on the toy. On the right side it's mirrored.
beats.on_screen: Left side, crop on fin logo
beats.label: fin logo

beats.narration_text: From behind, the cream engine bell and its cluster of dark nozzles. Grok Bot's own review says this bell is too big. Keep that in mind.
beats.label: engine bell

beats.narration_text: From the top, the long body, the fin strip down the spine, and the wings. From the front, the cross-section and the visor. This is the weakest view: the nose is too narrow and pointed next to the toy.
beats.label: plan shape, cross-section

beats.narration_text: Close up: the visor frame and glass, the turret dome with its barrel and antenna, and the side vent with its rivets and the wing ring.
beats.label: details

beats.narration_text: By the model's own README: 206 objects, about 109 thousand triangles, 13 materials, built from Python in Blender 4.2, run headless. Those numbers describe the asset. They don't measure how much it looks like the ship.
beats.on_screen: Stats card beside the side view, labelled 'reported by README'
beats.label: reported stats

beats.narration_text: The review history. At round 12, Grok Bot scored itself four out of ten. Professor Bear said, pretty good, maybe a six out of ten, but it could use another round. Round 13 skipped the hull, because of Grok Bot's own instruction. Round 15 scores five and a half. Professor Bear's verdict on it is still pending.
beats.label: r12 vs r15

beats.narration_text: What it isn't: a static model. No moving parts, no interior, no rig. It was matched to photos of one toy, not to the show's drawings.
beats.label: limitations

beats.narration_text: Recap. A strong side silhouette, good details, a front that's too narrow and an engine bell that's too big. Fifteen rounds, and the verdict on the last one is still open.
beats.on_screen: Recap card over the side view

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Open the gallery, put the front view beside the toy photo, and write down the one change you'd make first.
Built by Grok Bot. Narration: the Liam voice.
beats.on_screen: Credit card: 'Built by Grok Bot' / 'Narration: the Liam voice'

beats.narration_text: The Planet Express Ship, Walked Through. At Nik Bear Brown.
beats.on_screen: Outro card per OUTRO-LOCK: exact title 'The Planet Express Ship, Walked Through', handle @NikBearBrown, one seeded mascot; spoken, no music, 1.0 s silent tail
